Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:

- We can accept limited audit rights; our standard DPA includes a scoped audit clause. We can discuss any specific narrow asks you have and note them in the redline.
- Subprocessors (high-level): AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), Google Cloud (europe-west1) for backups, Datadog (logs/metrics), Sentry (error telemetry), Segment (telemetry routing), and Stripe for billing. If you need complete contractual names/addresses we can provide that in the DPA appendix.
- Transfers: we primarily rely on EU SCCs for transfers out of the EEA and certain dataflow agreements. For customers who require a specific mechanism we can add contract language or provide a Data Transfer Addendum.

I'm attaching our SOC 2 Type II summary and a redacted pen test excerpt. Please review and share your Word redlines. If it helps, I can upload our DPA draft to DocuSign as a PowerForm and send you a signing link once legal confirms final text.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Team — forwarding BlueRidge's initial ask; they say procurement wants Word redlines. They attached our SOC2 and pen test excerpts (sent to them) and will return their edits in a Word doc.

Key negotiation points to watch for:
- Audit clause: BlueRidge may push for an expansive audit right — we should push to keep it scoped (third-party assessor, limited frequency, and notice).
- Subprocessor acceptance: they may request prior notice for certain categories — agree to notice + opt-out only for high-risk subprocessor types.
- Data transfers: confirm that SCCs are acceptable; if they insist on a contract amendment, we can offer a Data Transfer Addendum.

I'm attaching the redlines they said they'd send once they return them — placeholder until we get the Word doc (they mentioned "BlueRidge_DPA_Redlines_20260822.docx"). Also linking the HubSpot deal for context: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BR-2026-0892

Grace

Attached are our Word redlines: BlueRidge_DPA_Redlines_20260822.docx. Key asks we flagged: expanded audit access (we proposed annual audits and right to interview personnel), right to require remediation timelines, and a carve-in for certain security metrics to be reported quarterly.

We also asked how Redwood handles access logs retention and whether Datadog/Sentry data is treated as subprocessed telemetry only (no customer PII). Please confirm retention windows and whether we can get an excerpted pen test report that references the most recent critical findings (redacted for vendor names as needed).

Laura

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the redlines and the specificity — that made review quicker. Legal has reviewed and responded to the main points:

- Audit clause: we can accept a single annual audit conducted by an independent third party with 30 days' notice; interviews limited to personnel with relevant responsibilities; remediation timelines will be committed to in good faith (we proposed 60 days for critical items).
- Telemetry/subprocessors: Datadog/Sentry/Segment are used for telemetry only; customer PII is not sent to them as part of normal operation. Retention windows are documented in the annex (30 days for raw telemetry, 365 days for aggregated logs).
- Data transfers: SCCs remain our standard; we will include a Data Transfer Addendum if you require additional assurances.

I've attached the SOC 2 summary and a pen test excerpt for procurement. Please note the pen test excerpt redacts vendor names but includes the summary of critical/major findings and remediation status.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached DPA tracker where we've captured accept/reject on each redline.
2) If you approve, sign via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&id=ABC12345 — once you sign we'll countersign and send the fully executed copy.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf; pen_test_excerpt.pdf; DPA_Final_Legal_Tracker.xlsx
